title: Restriction to the normalized exceptional system adjunction
statement: For D,l,E,X,Y,f,c as in integral reconstruction, fix rX:Reconstruction l E X and any s:Systems l E c [def-sf-exceptional-integral-reconstruction-interfaces]. The actual coordinate system functors s.left and s.exceptional preserve normalized strict constructible systems with common finite cohomological and Tor intervals and have the specified restricted adjunction, compatible origins and transpose equation: Nonempty (SystemAdjunction l E c s). This is the normalized restriction of the already existing system adjunction, not a construction of an integral realization.

proof.text: The middle scheme is finite type, hence Noetherian; its open factor is quasi-compact. The fixed finite evaluations identify both outputs with finite exceptional operations, which supply common cohomological and Tor bounds independent of the coefficient level.

proof.text: Constructible origin and the uniform lower bound provide the source and target origin assertions. The transported right operation preserves normalization. For the left operation, rX writes every normalized input as actual reduction of its limit; integral compact-support comparisons identify every successive transition adjunct with a composite of isomorphisms. Transport back along the reconstruction counit.

lean.statement:
theorem exceptionalIntegralNormalizedAdjunction
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f)
    (rX : Reconstruction l E X) (s : Systems l E c) :
    Nonempty (SystemAdjunction l E c s)
